lead_profile_text: Looking to buy a property for short term letting
property_situation: Buying a 2-bed city-centre apartment (Jewellery Quarter edge) as a buy-to-let run as short-term lets rather than ASTs. Offer submitted, awaiting acceptance; a second property also identified but Powell Street is the priority. Has an approval in principle with a generic lender (not the one he intends to use). Monday mortgage estimate £571.65/month.
property_type: 2-bed apartment in a managed high-rise block (Altitude), leasehold
primary_blocker: Purchase not agreed — offer out awaiting acceptance, then mortgage and completion; lead had not yet read the report in depth
language_signals: the Powell Street apartment that I really want to focus on
As a buy-to-let investment and do short-term lettings rather than the ASTs
this is not a guaranteed rent arrangement, is it?
I haven't really had an in-depth look at this report myself
the first stage for me is getting the purchase actually completed
do you do the high, medium, low weekly projection?

delay_signals.trigger_phrase: at the moment I'm trying to purchase the property, so I've got an offer out at the moment, and hopefully I'll be successful on that
delay_signals.context: Opening answer on his situation; later: 'the first stage for me is getting the purchase actually completed'
delay_signals.timeline_given: No date — offer not yet accepted; Zac to touch base around December 2026 if no update

meeting_flow.opening_phrase: I thought I'd start just by sort of understanding a bit on your current situation and situation with the property. You know, then we can go through the figures and our service, see if it lines up with what you're looking for.
meeting_flow.pivot_to_business: Okay, all right, nice. Well, I can go through the figures then and see if it sort of lines up with what you've projected your side, or we can go through it together.
meeting_flow.income_intro: So that's about 52,000 a year. Now we've got a net revenue, which is what you can expect as a payout, of about £2,200 per month.
meeting_flow.how_it_works_transition: Yeah, yeah, so it's a fully managed service. So to give you an idea of what that includes
meeting_flow.pre_close_setup: A couple of things to probably be aware of when doing a purchase which you might need our help with is the first one, when you go into a broker, they're going to need some kind of income projection.
meeting_flow.meeting_2_ask: Obviously, if the sale goes through, drop me a WhatsApp or an email or something like that, and we pick up next stages. And if not, if you don't hear from me, I'll probably touch base sort of December or something

lead_responses.what_lead_said: Is that after all like, fees, agency fees ... is that after Stayful's fees?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Yes — the only things to pay out of that are the mortgage and bills.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: And council tax and whatnot, things like that.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: This is not a guaranteed rent arrangement, is it? ... Do you do guaranteed rent?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: No, it's a projection — normally within about 10% either way. We do guaranteed rent for some properties but wouldn't for Birmingham.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: Got you, got you. Yeah, that's fair.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: How does it work? Is my property listed on Stayful's website, or does Stayful fully manage it?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Fully managed: Airbnb, Booking.com and our direct site; dynamic pricing, guest screening, deposits, check-ins, cleaning, repairs. You handle mortgage, bills and compliance; three tools — calendar, messaging app, monthly statement with payout 1st-5th.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: Do you do the high, medium, low weekly projection? ... what stage do you say you can provide that? ... if we can do it now, could we do it now?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Yes, signed by a director as brokers require — but get the offer accepted first and do it at the lending stage with the lender you'll actually use, otherwise you can pay for one that's wasted.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: Okay, yeah, no, that's good to know.

conversion_gaps.gap: Pre-purchase eligibility checks not raised: the mortgage product must permit short letting (standard BTL often doesn't) and the Altitude lease/building rules must allow short lets
conversion_gaps.evidence: Lead is at AIP stage with a generic lender and buying into a managed block; neither topic came up on the call
conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: For every PURCH lead buying a flat, ask about lender product and lease short-let clauses before completion — raised in the action plan

conversion_gaps.gap: Pre-qualifier concerns (income consistency/quiet months, damage or theft, input on maintenance, nervous about early weeks) were not addressed directly on the call
conversion_gaps.evidence: Monday long_text_mm2pse8d: 'Income picture: Still have concerns about quiet months ... Biggest worry about guests: Damage or theft ... First booking timing: Still nervous about the early weeks'; action plan S3: 'Whether the income is really achievable'
conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Read presentation responses before the call and open with the lead's stated worries — especially when the lead is quiet and says little

conversion_gaps.gap: January shown as the peak month (£4,216) and September trough (~£700) without explanation; deck headline net (£27,204) disagrees with its own forecast array (£31,200)
conversion_gaps.evidence: "Peak month being sort of around £4,000, which is actually sending in January, which is a little bit surprising if I'm honest."
conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Sanity-check seasonality and headline-vs-forecast consistency before the meeting; anchor on the annual total

conversion_gaps.gap: Lead had barely read the report and said little — engagement low, decision entirely gated on the purchase
conversion_gaps.evidence: "I haven't really had an in-depth look at this report myself"
conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Use the signed broker income projection as the re-engagement trigger once the offer is accepted

zac_language.numbers_framing: Gross → net payout → ADR/occupancy → worst (September) and best (January) months, flagging the odd January peak himself
zac_language.objection_handling_pattern: Short, honest answers (no guaranteed rent in Birmingham); adds value around the lead's actual next step (broker projection timing) instead of pushing for a decision

what_they_focused_on: Whether net is after all fees
Signed income projection for his broker and its timing
what_they_needed_most: Getting the offer accepted and the purchase completed
A broker-acceptable signed income projection at the lending stage
Reassurance on quiet months and damage (pre-qualifier answers)
what_fell_flat: Nothing overtly — engagement was simply low because the report hadn't been read
profile_psychology_intersection.recommended_meeting_adjustment: For early-stage PURCH leads with an offer still out, keep the meeting short, surface lender-product and lease short-let checks before completion, address the pre-qualifier worries explicitly, and set the broker projection as the concrete re-engagement point
